scenes.title: UNION ALL
scenes.narration: UNION ALL combines the rows of two queries into one result set and keeps every row, including duplicates.

scenes.title: How UNION ALL behaves
bullets: It concatenates both result sets without deduplication.
Duplicate rows are preserved rather than removed.
It is faster because no sort or hash pass is needed.
scenes.narration: UNION ALL simply appends the rows of the second query onto the first with no deduplication step. Any duplicate rows survive intact instead of being collapsed. Because there is no need to sort or hash to find duplicates, it is noticeably faster than plain UNION.

scenes.title: UNION versus UNION ALL

left.title: UNION
points: Requires a sort or hash pass

scenes.narration: UNION removes duplicates but pays for it with a sort or hash pass, which slows down on large sets. UNION ALL skips that work and returns every row exactly as produced. Choose UNION ALL when duplicates are impossible or when you actually want to keep them.

scenes.title: Merging monthly sales logs
scenes.code:
SELECT order_id, amount, 'January' AS month
FROM sales_jan

UNION ALL

SELECT order_id, amount, 'February' AS month
FROM sales_feb;
scenes.narration: Each query pulls orders from a separate monthly table and tags them with a month label. Since an order id cannot appear in both January and February, duplicates are impossible, making UNION ALL the correct and faster choice. The result is a complete log of every order across both months.

scenes.text: Default to UNION ALL and only use UNION when you specifically need duplicate elimination. This avoids paying the sorting cost when it buys you nothing.
scenes.narration: As a habit, reach for UNION ALL first and switch to UNION only when you truly need duplicates removed. This keeps you from paying the sorting cost in cases where it provides no benefit.
